subject: gl.join to combine three genlight objects?

messages.author: db110882830e3322
messages.subject: gl.join to combine three genlight objects?
parts:
Hello everyone,

Can anyone please suggest a solution to combine three datasets from the same Diversity Arrays service, where the files have been split due to size limitations? The three datasets each contain the same individuals and so have the same individual metadata, but different numbers of SNPs.

The data reads in fine into dartR from the three csv files and produces three genlight objects (gl.data.a, gl.data.b, gl.data.c). We can join any two of the three datasets together into a new genlight object using gl.join.

But what is the solution to join all three together without running into rbind(deparse.level) errors where the numbers of columns of arguments do not match? I believe this is a different issue than a previous conversation about rbind.genlight (26 Feb), as in the current case each genlight object contains the same individuals and the intent is not to reduce the number of SNPs (yet).

Extremely grateful for your help,
Thanks,
Caroline.

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: gl.join to combine three genlight objects?
parts:
Hi Caroline,

The process to join three datasets could be for example:

library(dartR)
gl.new <- gl.join(gl.data.a, gl.data.b)
gl.new <- gl.join(gl.new, gl.data.c)

Please let us know whether this worked for you.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: gl.join to combine three genlight objects?
parts:
Hi Caroline,

Maybe you are using an older version of dartR. To install the latest version, in which this problem has been solved, you can try the following:

# library required to install from github
library(devtools)
# installing beta version of dartR
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@beta",build_manual = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)

# if you are working with R-studio restart your session with menu Session -> Restart R

library(dartR)

gl.data.new <- gl.join(gl.data.a, gl.data.b)
gl.data.new <- gl.join(gl.data.new, gl.data.c)

Please let us know whether this worked for you.

Cheers,
Luis
